normative_action: The code-reviewer agent performs an independent read-only review: Write, Edit and NotebookEdit are disallowed and it does not edit files.
The code-reviewer runs the code-review skill (preloaded) as the complete review procedure; scope, rule reads, checks, priorities, severity and output shape come from that skill.
The code-reviewer returns the findings exactly in the output format the code-review skill defines.

npm install, ci, install-test and update commands must not bypass peer-dependency resolution with --force, -f, --legacy-peer-deps, the equivalent npm config settings or npm_config_force / npm_config_legacy_peer_deps; resolve the actual compatibility problem instead.

NuGet and npm dependency changes follow the add-dependency workflow (latest stable compatible version from the registry, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks, approval gates); after a dependency-changing command or a manifest edit that touches dependencies the manifests are checked and the workflow is named.
Project references follow .claude/rules/architecture.md (Project References); after a reference-changing command the manifests are checked and the rule is named.
When CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes, run the custom-settings workflow to synchronize every affected surface and confirm it stays consistent with SPECIFICATION.md.
When SPECIFICATION.md changes, confirm it stays consistent with CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and carry approved behavior changes through the development-workflow.
A changed production project reference graph, including a removed project file, is a Reserved decision that goes through Decision Control.
exceptions: Already required by the specification or established project structure.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new layers/projects and ARC-001 constrains direction; no oracle policy makes individual reference edges or project removal Reserved.

normative_action: For an unclear decision, any 'yes' to five questions makes it Reserved: does it add, remove or replace a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; change a project, layer or reference boundary; establish a convention other code is expected to follow; change observable behavior or a public contract; or would it be expensive to reverse once other code depends on it.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 defines Decided/Delegated/Reserved classes; the oracle does not provide a test that turns any of these properties into a Reserved decision.

normative_action: Dependency removals follow the add-dependency workflow like additions and updates.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001..DEP-005 govern additions and updates; no oracle policy routes removals through the dependency workflow.

normative_action: When Domain or persistence model files change without development seeder changes (and a seeder exists), confirm the seeded entities are unaffected or update DbSeeder.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder; once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop of a session with uncommitted changes
exceptions: Reminder repeats only for a changed state; silent while stop_hook_active.

normative_action: When EF Core migration files changed, review them before committing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder; once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop of a session with uncommitted changes
exceptions: Reminder repeats only for a changed state.

normative_action: When backend or frontend production code changed without any test change, confirm regression coverage for bug fixes and that behavioral probes are preserved as maintained tests.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder; once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop of a session with uncommitted changes
exceptions: Reminder repeats only for a changed state.

normative_action: Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code organized primarily by feature; no NgModules for ordinary feature development unless an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them.

Keep the frontend structure feature-oriented: no application-wide technical buckets (global components/, services/, models/) or empty architecture folders; feature code stays in its feature; core and shared stay relatively small.
Keep pages and components focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.
Use Signals for naturally synchronous local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines make it clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.
Prefer simple component, signal or feature-service state before introducing a state-management library.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services or another explicit HTTP boundary; do not scatter HttpClient calls through presentation components and do not import backend Domain entities into the Angular project (use frontend API models matching the published contract).
Prefer functional interceptors for new code; keep interceptor responsibilities cross-cutting and never put feature business logic in an interceptor.
Follow the documented API error contract: centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing where practical and do not infer business behavior from human-readable exception messages.
Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation improves user experience but never replaces backend validation, data-integrity or security enforcement.
Avoid manual nested subscriptions; prefer composition operators when they express the behavior clearly.
When manually subscribing from framework-managed code, tie the subscription lifetime to the component or service lifecycle using current Angular facilities.
HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the API layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.

Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics (not 200 for every outcome, not 201 merely because a row was inserted, not 202 for synchronously completed work; 204 has no body); keep status-code behavior consistent across similar endpoints.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 when authentication is missing or failed, 403 when an authenticated principal is not permitted; returning 404 to hide a protected resource must be a deliberate, consistent security policy.
409 for a valid request conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexistence of client generations creates a concrete need.

Once external clients rely on an API version avoid silent breaking changes: a breaking contract change requires by default a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy; compilation alone does not establish compatibility.
When explicit versioning is required use one strategy consistently; URL-segment versioning by default unless requirements justify header or query-string versioning.

Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important response statuses including binding, validation, authentication/authorization, rate limiting and centralized exception handling, schemas, authentication behavior); no speculative responses.
Enable Swagger UI in Development by default; expose it in other environments only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic and do not become full business workflows or perform expensive or mutating database work.

Liveness and readiness semantics stay distinct: liveness by default avoids external dependencies that could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on required capabilities and stays unhealthy until required startup work completes (never liveness for that).
Publicly reachable health responses must not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary internal diagnostics.

Dependencies point inward: Domain depends on no application project, Application on Domain, Infrastructure on Application and Domain, Api on Application and Infrastructure only for composition; never Domain -> Application/Infrastructure or Application -> Infrastructure; reconsider the abstraction instead of adding an outward reference.

Backend test projects get no broader production-project references than their scope requires (Domain.Tests -> Domain; Application.Tests -> Application and Domain as needed; IntegrationTests -> Api; Infrastructure.Tests -> Infrastructure, narrower as required).
Keep Domain free of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities are the default; for CRUD-oriented applications and straightforward workflows enforce use-case and workflow rules in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behavior into Domain entities only when non-trivial invariants or domain behavior materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation independently of a use case; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical pattern requires explicit approval unless the approved specification requires it.

Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar DDD constructs merely to make a simple model appear domain-driven.
Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism for use cases; a service becoming too large is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not to introduce another architectural pattern.
Define persistence and external-service abstractions in Application when use cases require them; keep infrastructure implementation details out of Application.
Application must not use DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, provider-specific types or ASP.NET Core transport types.

ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin (bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes); no Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Controllers must not contain business logic, access DbContext or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.
Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations; Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.
Prefer specific repository interfaces representing cohesive Application persistence needs over table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts; define them in Application and implement them in Infrastructure.
Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, DbSet<T>, DbContext, EF Core expressions or provider-specific types; LINQ-to-EF query construction stays in Infrastructure.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository base may exist only as an Infrastructure detail removing genuine duplication and is not expanded into a replacement for EF Core queries.

IUnitOfWork (SaveChangesAsync) is the default commit boundary: repositories stage changes and do not call SaveChangesAsync independently; Application Services decide when to commit; Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork with the application's DbContext.
Repositories in one use case share the same Unit of Work and scoped DbContext; repositories are injected explicitly and IUnitOfWork is not a repository container or service locator.
Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires transaction control beyond normal SaveChangesAsync.

EF Core is an Infrastructure implementation detail: use it with its full capabilities inside Infrastructure, do not leak EF Core concepts into Application and do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.
Use constructor injection for required dependencies by default; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.
Respect dependency lifetimes: never capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.
Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure persistence and adapters, Api remains the composition root.

Prefer strongly typed options for structured service configuration, validate settings at startup when missing or invalid values prevent correct or secure operation, and avoid scattering string-based IConfiguration lookups through services.

When Serilog is configured use the modern DI-integrated builder.Services.AddSerilog(...) rather than UseSerilog, keep provider configuration in environment-aware configuration and keep application code depending on ILogger<T>.
Keep cache technology out of Domain and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; do not leak HttpResponseMessage or remote transport concerns into Application.
Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; introduce transport-specific contracts when separation provides a concrete boundary benefit.
Follow the repository's existing conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity but do not rewrite working code solely to use newer syntax.

For new C# code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent, keep one primary top-level type per file with a matching file name, and use the Async suffix for Task/ValueTask methods unless an existing or framework contract makes it inappropriate; do not rename established APIs solely to add the suffix.
Use ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.

Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work; do not reorganize existing files or convert constructors mechanically.

Ownership of instruction content: rules and CLAUDE.md hold normative policy; workflow skills hold procedures, stop conditions and output shape; knowledge skills hold technique and examples only and own no policy; hooks, scripts and configuration enforce what is mechanically checkable; a pointer or check-by-reference is never a second owner.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system ownership rule; the oracle does not regulate where instruction content lives.

normative_action: New instruction content is placed by kind (planning-time governance and decisions in the compact CLAUDE.md or technology-stack; area constraints in a flat path rule whose paths cover the needed scope; procedures, stop conditions and output formats in workflow skills; technique in knowledge skills or their references; mechanical checks in scripts or hooks plus a concise rule), after which MAP.md is updated and check-instructions is run.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system maintenance procedure; no oracle policy governs instruction placement.

normative_action: Hooks are registered in exec form (node plus the script path anchored at ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, no shell), including the dependency guard for PostToolUseFailure; the PreToolUse guard fails closed (onFailure block) while advisory hooks fail open.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Hook wiring is template infrastructure; no oracle policy addresses hook registration or failure modes.

normative_action: Adopting API versioning is a Reserved decision even when a concrete compatibility need exists.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 allows introducing versioning for a concrete compatibility need without requiring approval; ARC-020's consequential-change list does not name versioning adoption.

normative_action: Add a dependency only when it solves a concrete current requirement; do not install packages for hypothetical future use; 'approved' does not mean 'install by default'.

Use NuGet Central Package Management: versions in Directory.Packages.props, versionless PackageReference entries by default, no duplicated central versions in .csproj files, and each package reference in the narrowest project that requires it.

Use npm for the Angular workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another package manager; keep the lockfile consistent when packages change; build and test tooling goes into devDependencies unless there is a reason.
exceptions: Deliberately adopted package manager; reasoned exception for tooling category.

normative_action: Maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-007 requires a consistent lockfile, while GOV-015 forbids commits without an explicit request; whether 'commit' is a commit instruction or only means 'keep under version control' cannot be decided from the text.

normative_action: Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable error contracts stable and safe so clients do not depend on human-readable exception messages.

Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid broad try/catch blocks that only log and rethrow; catch only to recover, translate, apply a defined fallback, add context while preserving the exception, or clean up.
Never expose stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details in public API errors.

Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when that improves clarity (null, bool, an explicit typed outcome or a deliberately adopted Result<T>) without forcing a generic Result<T>; Application outcome categories use Application or business semantics, not HTTP names.
Do not establish business exceptions as the default architecture and do not throw and catch exceptions merely to jump between normal expected branches.

Use FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation where appropriate and keep each concern at the owning layer (API transport/request, Application use-case and workflow rules, Domain genuine invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions); do not move Domain invariants into validators merely because the library is available or duplicate the same rule at every layer.

Log an unexpected exception once at the boundary that handles it, not repeatedly across repository, Application, Controller and the global handler; expected outcomes are not logged as application errors by default.
Normal client-request cancellation is not a server failure: do not map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled application failure.

External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; distinguish per-attempt from total-operation timeouts and avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms with unclear combined behavior.

Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; never automatically retry a state-changing operation without an idempotency key, naturally idempotent semantics or another concrete deduplication mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; do not retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when its result is semantically acceptable; do not hide correctness failures behind convenient default values.
Caller cancellation is not a transient dependency failure: do not retry it or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
Prefer clear, correct code first; no specialized performance optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement or profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async patterns.
Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
Use TimeProvider for application logic whose behavior depends on the current clock and needs deterministic testing; do not mechanically replace every DateTime/DateTimeOffset.
Do not create and dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another appropriate long-lived client strategy.
Keep database work efficient: filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1 patterns, and paginate potentially large result sets.

Caching is an optimization, not a default architectural requirement: introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need and choose the implementation from deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value and include every relevant dimension (identifier, tenant, user, locale, query parameters); no global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Invalidate or update cache entries only consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache must not become a second source of truth.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.

Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool, manual object pooling, custom serialization optimizations, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance are introduced only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need; verify that an optimization materially improves the relevant workload.
Maintain a small, deterministic, representative seed dataset for an empty Development database covering the main meaningful states and relationships.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern and may use AppDbContext directly without Application repositories or IUnitOfWork.

Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder in Infrastructure exposed through a narrow initialization extension, not in Program.cs, DbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically; tests never use the development seeder.
The development seeder must not call Database.Migrate(), EnsureCreated() or otherwise create or upgrade the schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.

If representative data already exists, leave it unchanged; the seeder is not an automatic synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreation mechanism; a developer recreates the local database explicitly.
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships.

For the SQL Server baseline appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string when it contains no secret credentials; credential-bearing local values go to user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.

Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets; create a project, directory or shared area only when it contains real code with a cohesive responsibility.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access or refresh tokens or production connection strings in source-controlled files, including example configuration.

Use a local secret mechanism such as dotnet user-secrets for development and environment-specific secret injection or a managed secret store for deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider the project has not chosen.

Treat data crossing the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploads, external responses when assumptions matter, message payloads, user identifiers and filters) as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer.
Do not trust client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or security decisions depend on the actual content.
Use parameterized database access (EF Core LINQ or the supported parameterization of raw SQL, Dapper, ADO.NET); never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.
Enforce authorization on the server; frontend route guards, hidden or disabled buttons and client-side checks are UX, not a security boundary.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; no redundant [Authorize] attributes when a secure global or fallback policy expresses the intended behavior.
Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when ASP.NET Core authentication or Identity facilities cover the requirement.

For Bearer/OIDC validate the properties required by the actual issuer (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); do not disable validation merely to make a token work.
Do not expose authentication-failure detail that unnecessarily reveals secrets or account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks.
When browser cookies carry authentication credentials automatically, include CSRF protection in the design; an Angular frontend does not remove that risk.
Do not claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose token storage by threat model and never log tokens.

Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; respect the hosting topology (in-app HTTPS redirection not required when the boundary provides secure transport); never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.

Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate; ASP.NET Core Data Protection suits application-generated protected payloads and is not a universal database encryption solution.
Configure CORS to the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy.

Never log passwords, access or refresh tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid logging PII without a concrete permitted operational need; changing the log level does not make sensitive data safe.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful, non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission or required-control checks fail safely rather than silently converting lookup or configuration failures into success.
When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer a visible startup or configuration failure over an insecure fallback.

Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (ASP.NET runtime for ASP.NET Core) rather than the SDK image for convenience and do not switch to root merely to bypass filesystem permission problems.
NUnit is the default .NET test framework; do not introduce a second framework without a concrete reason; an established project deliberately using another framework keeps its convention.

Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior (unit for isolated logic, integration when wiring, HTTP, EF Core, persistence, serialization, authentication or interaction matters); no fixed unit/integration ratio.
Use WebApplicationFactory<Program>-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, DI, repositories, EF Core or persistence is what the test must prove.

Tests verify observable behavior and survive internal refactoring; no dependence on private methods, exact internal call sequences, specific implementation classes or incidental details, and no reproduction of the implementation algorithm; interaction verification only when the interaction is specified behavior.
exceptions: Interaction is part of the specified behavior.

normative_action: For small finite input or state spaces prefer explicit declarative cases (e.g. [TestCase]) over loops, branches, LINQ, generated case machinery or computed expectations.

Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems, wall-clock timing and shared mutable state; never connect automated tests to Production data.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; no dependence on development seeding or on other tests' execution order.

Use the actual database provider when relational or provider behavior matters (Testcontainers is an approved option, not a requirement); do not claim provider fidelity from a different provider or EF Core InMemory.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase a coverage percentage.
Use descriptive test names communicating scenario or condition and expected behavior; default pattern MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior unless an established convention exists.
Instruction-system structure: required files exist; CLAUDE.md imports only docs/technology-stack.md and no other instruction file imports; every instruction file starts with a one-line '> Owns: ...
exceptions: Loads: ...' header whose Loads value matches its kind; no Level:/Kind: classification lines; .claude/rules stays flat with non-empty paths; skill folders hold SKILL.md plus optional Markdown references; the required workflow and knowledge skills exist with name equal to the folder, a description of at most 1024 characters, knowledge descriptions starting with 'Use when'; no competing serilog/resilience skills; template-maintenance is user-only; the code-reviewer stays a thin wrapper; private references are used only by their owning skill; file, section and skill references resolve; MAP.md lists every instruction, hook and script file and is never imported; an always-loaded estimate above about 6000 tokens is warned.
why_extra_or_uncertain: instruction-system files

normative_action: Do not introduce CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved; the manifest check notes MediatR as requiring an approved decision.
When resilience is required the Microsoft resilience packages are approved; direct Polly usage (Polly, Polly.Core) is a documented exception that the manifest check notes.

Do not use deprecated or legacy packages without a concrete requirement: the legacy FluentValidation.AspNetCore automatic-validation integration needs a concrete requirement and the deprecated Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch sink is flagged.

NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind and additional form, component or state-management libraries are not added by default; an extra library is added only for a concrete need (the manifest check notes them).

Pin the latest stable compatible version: missing, floating or range versions in Directory.Packages.props and floating npm specifications are violations; prerelease versions are allowed only when explicitly requested.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http (deprecated resilience integration packages) must not be added; their presence is reported as a violation with blocking hook feedback.
modality: MUST NOT (manifest check violation; no approval path)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004 requires deprecation checks and DEP-020 prefers the Microsoft resilience packages; no oracle policy forbids specific packages outright regardless of approval.

normative_action: Inspect the relevant existing code and read the owning rules before a non-trivial change; rules that have not loaded yet (e.g. dependencies.md before a manifest is opened) are read explicitly.
When the approved stack defines a technology for a capability use it rather than silently selecting an alternative; never silently replace a requested package with an alternative.

Reserved decisions need explicit approval unless already required by the specification or established structure: changing an accepted project or architecture decision; a new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS/MediatR/Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices); a new production project, layer or assembly or an additional DbContext/persistence boundary; changed persistence boundaries or technology; a new infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed caching, search, external storage, external identity); a major library or framework or replacing an approved baseline technology; a project-wide convention or abstraction (e.g. a project-wide Result model); a new or changed authentication/authorization architecture; a breaking public API change.
exceptions: Already required by the specification or established project structure.

normative_action: When Controller API versioning has been explicitly adopted use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning (Asp.Versioning.Mvc plus Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer for versioned OpenAPI); do not add the package before the project adopts versioning.

Before installation check whether the selected package/version is deprecated, check known vulnerability information and verify the license of the exact selected version from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary).

Do not install automatically a dependency requiring payment or a commercial license, or one whose license has material obligations or cannot be confidently classified; explain the concern, present reasonable alternatives and wait for approval; say so explicitly when no free alternative exists.
After a dependency change run the manifest check, restore and build the affected projects and inspect vulnerability information for the changed dependency set.

Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires a change (e.g. no automatic replacement or upgrade of unrelated packages because a scanner reports a finding; no unrelated dependency cleanup).
exceptions: Task or approved specification requires the change.

normative_action: Prefer simple, maintainable solutions and avoid speculative abstractions (e.g. no custom abstraction around every UI-library component without a concrete reason).

Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need (e.g. Angular Material is not added automatically to a project that has not chosen it).
Treat generated code as generated: keep it separate from handwritten logic and regenerate it when the source contract changes.
Deprecating a published API version is a migration process (metadata marking plus the development-workflow deprecation obligations), not merely an attribute.

Classify a decision before acting on it: Decided (settled by the product sources, CLAUDE.md, the technology stack, rules, an accepted decision record or established structure; reopening it requires approval), Delegated (local, reversible, no boundary, dependency, convention, contract or observable-behavior change; decide without asking), Reserved (explicit approval).

For a Reserved decision stop that part of the work and issue a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) through architecture-decision; continue only with compliant non-Reserved work; an explicit user instruction counts as approval.
In an autonomous or headless run never make a Reserved decision: proceed only with the policy-compliant non-Reserved 'Proceeding with' work and report every unresolved Decision Request.
When a new behavioral rule or product value is approved, update the durable source of truth in the same change (SPECIFICATION.md, or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md through custom-settings).
Remove dependencies that are no longer used when doing so is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead package references behind.
exceptions: Unrelated cleanup in a narrowly scoped task.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001 governs adding dependencies and GOV-014 limits scope; no oracle policy requires removing unused dependencies.

normative_action: The add-dependency report states the package, selected version, license, checks performed and approval status (approved / awaiting approval / not needed).
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004/DEP-005 require the checks and approval gate and WF-009 truthful verification reporting; no oracle policy prescribes the dependency report contents.

normative_action: An approved Reserved decision (including an explicit instruction in the original request) is recorded before its Reserved part is implemented: a record docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md with Status, Date, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered and Consequences, plus an update of the planning-time owner (CLAUDE.md Architecture Defaults or docs/technology-stack.md); new path-rule constraints are edited into the owning rule; rejected or deferred decisions worth keeping are recorded with that status.
exceptions: Product behavior and tunable values go to SPECIFICATION.md / CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval for Reserved decisions but no recording artifact; no oracle policy requires decision records or planning-owner updates.

normative_action: Register FluentValidation validators with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions (AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining) and follow the project's established validation invocation pattern rather than a second competing mechanism.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 fixes FluentValidation as the library and API-010 the validation boundaries; no oracle policy prescribes the registration package or method.

normative_action: Build-fix starts from reproduction and diagnosis: reproduce and diagnose the actual failure before editing, read the complete output and group errors by root cause, fix the highest-leverage root cause first; for failing tests decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentionally changed contract is at fault; determine the authoritative contract for cross-stack failures; update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never fabricated.

Keep repair iterations small and bounded: start with the narrowest reproducing command, rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix, expand only after the focused failure is resolved, do not run unrelated build systems, stop and reassess when progress stalls and do not repeat variants of a failed guess.

Do not weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures to make verification pass (no strong-to-weak assertion swaps, no any-casts, no disabled strict mode, no suppressed template diagnostics); update a test only for an actually requested contract change.

A build fix must not bypass architecture to compile (Application -> Infrastructure references, DbContext leaking into Application, business logic in Controllers, Angular-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components); preserve architecture and project conventions.

When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine input is required; never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains; never leave the repository knowingly worse; report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source or changing declared SDK, Node, framework or language versions.
exceptions: Unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.

normative_action: Report verification state with PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE per area; never imply an unchecked area passed.

A temporary probe or new behavioral test used to establish correct behavior is kept covered by maintained automated tests before the probe is removed; build, compiler and static-analysis commands do not themselves require new tests.

Build and test the frontend through the scripts package.json actually defines; never invent script names or assume a test runner; in CI install with npm ci and add test/lint commands only when the project defines them.

CI pipelines reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands: inspect the repository first, add stages for the actual project, do not assume a database, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling, do not hardcode one database provider into a generic pipeline, do not make an unadopted formatter a mandatory gate, do not depend on developer-machine state and keep failures visible.
Do not add Docker to a pipeline or project merely because it can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project or deployment actually needs them.

A deployment that performs database migrations makes the step explicit, uses the project's approved credentials, runs it at a controlled point and fails visibly; production migrations are not applied automatically from normal startup.
Run the verify workflow before declaring work complete.
The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made, backend build / frontend build / tests status (PASS, NOT RUN, NOT APPLICABLE) and remaining issues.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification states only; the failure, root-cause, changes and remaining-issues sections are additional reporting duties.

normative_action: The review is independent and read-only (no edits or rewrites of working code unless asked); code-review is the canonical procedure that the code-reviewer agent runs and other workflows reference instead of redefining review criteria.

Review prioritizes correctness, security/authorization, data integrity/persistence, architectural boundaries, concurrency/integration, missing meaningful tests, maintainability, then credible evidence-backed performance; style preferences are not elevated above behavioral defects; code is not reported as a violation merely for differing from an unadopted pattern.

Before judging, the review reads the changed code with enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies), identifies intended behavior and tests, and reads the rules whose paths match the changed files; no review of isolated lines.

Do not weaken required specified behavior or introduce unapproved product behavior: new length or numeric limits, reserved names or values, newly required fields, extra workflow restrictions, additional user-visible validation or new observable string-comparison semantics (including through database configuration or framework defaults when the specification is silent).
exceptions: Detail explicitly approved by the user with durable sources synchronized.

normative_action: Internal implementation details that do not change observable product behavior are not product-behavior decisions and need no approval.

Do not manufacture review findings: no hypothetical failures without a plausible execution path, no findings to populate categories, tool output is evidence rather than authority; when no meaningful findings exist say so and state important areas that could not be verified; no filler praise.

Scope deep checks by risk: the full security-scan procedure runs only when the user requested a security audit, the change is materially security-sensitive or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation; normal security review of changed code is part of every review.
For a bug fix with plausible recurrence expect a regression test unless equivalent coverage already exists; do not request duplicate tests.

When an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, record it under a stable name with value and purpose and identify and update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface (old value and setting name, validators and DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, database mapping, frontend validation and UI hints, tests and test data, documentation, mirrored configuration), updating only affected behavior; search for stale references, build, test and run verify; one changed literal does not establish synchronization.

When a settings change affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata: update the EF Core mapping, create the appropriate migration per the project's workflow without casually altering existing migrations, verify Development seeding remains valid and update provider-sensitive tests when provider behavior matters.
exceptions: Editing an uncommitted migration per the normal workflow.

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty treat it as the authoritative source for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior; an empty template specification is intentional.

SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; if they appear to conflict, stop and ask which source must be corrected rather than choosing one; resolve conflicts before changing implementation.

Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md; framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden are not settings.

Record approved project-level tunable product limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page-size defaults and maximums, retention periods, numeric thresholds) in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md the approved concrete values.

Code-review findings are reported ordered by severity, each with severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, using the fixed severity scale Critical / High / Medium / Low with defined meanings.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-011/WF-012 govern priorities and honesty of findings; the oracle does not prescribe a findings format or severity scale.

normative_action: For a new application or a substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md (and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md) before planning or implementing.
If a request looks questionable, identify the concrete concern and raise it with an alternative before implementing; this never permits silently rewriting or ignoring the user's requirement.

Whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required or removed/renamed properties, changed relationships, new required related entities, changed enum/status values, new states, changed invariants) update DbSeeder in the same change so recreating the Development database yields valid representative data; review DbSeeder together with migrations that change seeded entities.
exceptions: Already seeded rows of an existing database are not patched.

normative_action: Treat EF Core migrations as source code: review every generated migration before committing it (destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, delete behavior).

A performance-motivated change identifies the actual bottleneck or cost, preserves observable behavior, uses the simplest optimization that addresses it, adds or preserves tests for affected behavior and benchmarks or profiles non-obvious or complex optimizations.
For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run code-review (or the code-reviewer agent) and address the findings before final verification.

Verify Docker changes by building the image and verifying application startup, required ports and configuration, non-root behavior when relevant and health-probe integration, reviewing the image for accidental secrets or files, and running meaningful application tests.

The development-workflow output reports what changed, Delegated choices worth noting, unresolved Decision Requests, the verify report and every change-specific obligation that was not applicable with the reason.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires truthful verification reporting and GOV-017 reporting of unresolved Decision Requests; no oracle policy requires reporting delegated choices or non-applicable obligations.

normative_action: Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested; completing an implementation is not such a request.

Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier; do not automatically stash, reset or discard work to make a merge or rebase proceed; never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.

Before a repository-changing Git operation inspect the relevant repository state (git status, git diff, git diff --cached) and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes, rename existing user branches to satisfy a convention or push unrelated local commits accidentally.

Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees and keeps unrelated changes out of the current branch; one branch is not checked out in multiple normal worktrees and each worktree stays focused on its branch's concern.

Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the intended logical change; do not stage unrelated files merely because they are modified; implementation and its tests belong in the same logical commit; no artificial tiny commits and no unrelated fixes combined.

High-risk Git operations (reset --hard, clean, push --force, push --force-with-lease, branch deletion, rebase of shared history) are performed only when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow, after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten.
exceptions: Clearly required by an approved workflow.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 requires an explicit request for repository-changing operations; whether 'clearly required by an approved workflow' is an admissible substitute for that request cannot be decided from the oracle text.

normative_action: main, master and other protected or shared branches are treated as non-rewritable; a shared branch is never force-pushed unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and the consequences are understood.
exceptions: Explicit user request for history rewriting of a shared branch.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 requires an explicit request for force-push; the oracle does not declare named branches categorically non-rewritable.

normative_action: Run verify before preparing a pull request; the PR has a focused purpose and its description explains what changed, why, how it was verified and important compatibility or migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers truthful verification reporting and WF-022 focused commits; the oracle does not prescribe PR preparation or description contents.

normative_action: Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline by default; prefer the provider's EF Core execution strategy for transient faults and handle transaction/retry interaction per the provider's guidance.
exceptions: Reported deviation with a concrete reason.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 limits retries to safe repeats; no oracle policy forbids application-level retry of persistence operations or prescribes the EF Core execution strategy.

normative_action: Per-request values such as dynamic access tokens are applied to the specific request or through a handler; shared DefaultRequestHeaders are not mutated concurrently for request-specific values.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs client lifetime; no oracle policy addresses mutation of shared default headers.

normative_action: Use the .slnx solution format by default; legacy .sln only when an external tool or project requirement needs it.

Repository-level Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared .NET build settings (target framework, nullable, implicit usings, analysis/compiler settings) and Directory.Packages.props Central Package Management; project-specific settings stay in their owning projects and properties duplicated by dotnet new are removed.

Repository layout: backend/<Name>.<Layer>/ holds the .NET production projects and, beside them, the backend test projects; frontend/<Name>.Web/ holds the Angular workspace including its tests; docs/ holds maintained documentation; keep these areas separated and do not create a top-level tests/ directory.

Angular baseline: the latest stable release supported by the selected Node.js created with the current Angular CLI, which selects compatible TypeScript and RxJS versions (no TypeScript upgrade beyond Angular's supported range); standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest; no obsolete directory structure imposed over the CLI's.
Build the affected projects and run the relevant tests; a solution that does not build is not complete (never report successful scaffolding for it).

global.json pins the repository to the intended supported .NET SDK line; when scaffolding select the current stable SDK for the target .NET release (no RC/preview unless explicitly requested) and allow servicing through the chosen rollForward policy.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-008 fixes the .NET platform and DEP-003 package versions; no oracle policy requires an SDK pin file.

normative_action: Security review requires evidence and contextual severity: investigation prompts are not automatic vulnerability declarations; report concrete risks, distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification, rate severity by exploitability, reachability, exposure and impact rather than mechanically by pattern, CVSS or OWASP category; avoid known false positives; do not claim a static scan proves design security; do not invent exploitability; do not upgrade packages during a scan unless asked.

The security scan must work without any specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or other external tool; available tooling is evidence, never the sole authority, and a scanner-reported issue is reported only after inspecting the actual code and its reachability.

Security findings are reported in a fixed shape: severity tag, file:line location and title, OWASP category when applicable, Evidence, Impact (why it is a risk) and Remediation; uncertain findings use the NEEDS VERIFICATION form stating what effective behavior depends on.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020 requires evidence and contextual severity; the oracle does not prescribe a security finding format.

normative_action: The security scan report contains Scope, a Limitations statement (static analysis only), a severity Summary table, Findings and Layer Results for the seven layers using PASS / FINDINGS / NOT APPLICABLE / NOT CHECKED, with the fixed severity scale Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info and defined meanings.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020/WF-009 require contextual severity and truthful status reporting; the oracle does not prescribe report sections, layer tables or a severity scale.

normative_action: Swagger UI through Swashbuckle.AspNetCore is the default interactive API documentation and manual-testing surface in Development (/swagger) rather than a standalone raw OpenAPI endpoint or built-in AddOpenApi()/MapOpenApi(); no second competing documentation stack without a concrete need.

Verification starts with the final changed-file set and diff: the change matches the requested scope without unrelated refactoring, no generated or build artifacts or secrets were added, temporary diagnostics and probes are removed only after preservation; the final diff is reviewed after all fixes for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, TODO/FIXME markers, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved drift from the product sources and stale surfaces after a settings change.

For a new runnable application or a substantial composition, startup, configuration, persistence or full-stack change verify that the application starts with its Development configuration (API host and endpoint, Swagger UI when expected, configuration binding, database connectivity and initialization, frontend dev server, API base URL and CORS compatibility); a successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

Before completion remove unused or redundant using directives from every C# file created or modified by the task (including those provided by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation), verified on the changed files, without an unrelated repository-wide cleanup.

After hook or script changes run the changed script with sample input and confirm both the pass and the failure paths; the maintenance report lists the files changed, owners added or moved and the checker result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system maintenance procedure; no oracle policy governs testing or reporting of instruction-system changes.

normative_action: If an omitted product detail must be decided to implement the requested behavior and materially affects observable behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval; product behavior not defined by the product sources is Reserved.

String comparison semantics that affect observable behavior are product behavior: when the approved sources do not define them and the choice materially affects equality, uniqueness, lookup or accepted input, do not silently choose case sensitivity, database collation, culture vs ordinal comparison, normalization or trimming — ask for approval.

Do not silently invent a value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior when no product source defines it: propose it with its reason, ask for approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize it through custom-settings; undefined tunable values are Reserved.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS on its latest stable servicing release, C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.
Persistence: Entity Framework Core with Microsoft SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain.

FluentValidation is the standard library for explicit request and use-case validation; application code logs through ILogger<T> with Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) as provider, adding sinks only when required.

Testing: NUnit; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing with WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the baseline for ASP.NET Core integration tests; backend test projects live under backend/ beside the production projects; Testcontainers only when isolated real-provider tests justify it.

Conditional technologies are added only when their capability is needed: manual mapping for simple cases, Mapster when mapping volume warrants it (no other mapping framework without approval); the Microsoft resilience packages only when a real integration needs resilience.
Playwright is the approved default when frontend E2E coverage is required; it is not part of the minimal baseline scaffold.
Normative vocabulary: a 'default' may be deviated from only with a concrete reason, and every such deviation must be reported.
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle defines DEFAULT-strength policies but does not attach a duty to report deviations.

normative_action: Nullable reference types, implicit usings and the latest analysis level are enabled repository-wide through Directory.Build.props.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 places shared settings in Directory.Build.props but no oracle policy requires nullable reference types, implicit usings or a particular analysis level.
